 ET Online Ahoi Ashtami 2026 will be observed on November 1. Check the puja muhurat, star-sighting time, vrat vidhi and traditional Ahoi Mata vrat katha. (AI Image) Ahoi Ashtami 2026 Tomorrow: Date, Puja Muhurat, Tara Darshan Time and Vrat Vidhi
 Ahoi Ashtami 2026: Ahoi Ashtami will be observed on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The festival is dedicated to Ahoi Mata, and mothers traditionally observe a fast for the health, happiness and long life of their children. The evening observance includes Ahoi Mata puja, the recitation of the Ahoi Ashtami vrat katha and prayers after sighting stars.
 For New Delhi, the Ahoi Ashtami puja muhurat is from 5:36 PM to 6:54 PM, while stars are expected to become visible around 6:00 PM. The Ashtami Tithi begins at 2:51 PM on November 1 and ends at 1:10 PM on November 2.
Here is everything to know about Ahoi Ashtami 2026, including the vrat procedure, puja samagri, fasting rules, tara darshan time and the traditional vrat katha. 
 Ahoi Ashtami 2026 Quick Guide 
 Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026
 Puja Muhurat: 5:36 PM to 6:54 PM
 Ashtami Tithi Begins: November 1, 2:51 PM
 Ashtami Tithi Ends: November 2, 1:10 PM
 Tara Darshan: Around 6:00 PM
 Vrat: Traditionally observed for the well-being of children
 Timings are based on the New Delhi Panchang. Local timings may vary.

 Ahoi Ashtami 2026 Puja Muhurat 
The Ahoi Ashtami puja is traditionally performed during the evening, around sunset. For New Delhi, the indicative puja muhurat on November 1, 2026, is from 5:36 PM to 6:54 PM.
 During this period, devotees worship Ahoi Mata and pray for their children's health, happiness and prosperity. The puja is generally performed at home, with the deity's image or a traditional drawing placed in the worship area.
The evening puja is followed by the recitation or listening of the Ahoi Ashtami vrat katha. Families may follow different ritual sequences according to their regional and household traditions.
 Ahoi Ashtami 2026 Tara Darshan Time 
Tara Darshan, or the sighting of stars, is an important part of Ahoi Ashtami. Traditionally, mothers observe the fast throughout the day and complete it after the evening puja and sighting of stars.
For New Delhi, stars are expected to become visible at approximately 6:00 PM on November 1, 2026. The timing may vary in other cities.
After sighting the stars, devotees traditionally offer arghya, or water, and pray for the well-being of their children. The fast is then completed according to the family's customary practices.
 Ahoi Ashtami Moonrise Time 
Some families follow the tradition of breaking the Ahoi Ashtami fast after sighting the Moon instead of stars.
For New Delhi, the expected moonrise is around 11:40 PM on November 1, 2026. This is considerably later than the evening star-sighting time.
Devotees should follow their family tradition and check the local moonrise timing if they observe the fast until Moon worship.
 Ahoi Ashtami Vrat Kaise Rakhein? Puja Vidhi and Fasting Rules
Ahoi Ashtami puja is performed to seek the blessings of Ahoi Mata for the well-being of children. The following is a general outline of the traditional observance.
 Begin the vrat: Devotees traditionally begin the fast after their morning routine, following the fasting customs observed in their family.
 Prepare the puja area: Clean the place of worship and arrange the image or traditional drawing of Ahoi Mata.
 Arrange the puja samagri: Keep the diya, flowers, roli, rice, water and other customary offerings ready.
 Perform the evening puja: Worship Ahoi Mata during the prescribed evening muhurat and offer prayers for the health and happiness of children.
 Listen to the vrat katha: Recite or listen to the traditional Ahoi Ashtami story as part of the puja.
 Offer arghya after tara darshan: After the stars become visible, offer water and perform the customary prayers.
 Complete the vrat: Break the fast according to the family's tradition, generally after the evening worship.
 Ahoi Ashtami Fast Process: What Should Devotees Do?
The Ahoi Ashtami fast is traditionally observed throughout the day, with the evening puja dedicated to Ahoi Mata. Devotees prepare the puja area, offer prayers, listen to the vrat katha and complete the observance according to their family customs.
Many families break the fast after sighting stars and offering arghya, while some follow the tradition of completing the fast after moonrise. Fasting practices, including whether food or water is consumed during the day, vary across households.
Devotees should follow their customary rituals and consider their health before undertaking a prolonged or waterless fast.
 Ahoi Ashtami Puja Samagri List 
The following items are commonly used for Ahoi Ashtami puja. The list can be adjusted according to regional and family traditions.
 Image or drawing of Ahoi Mata
 Puja thali
 Diya and cotton wicks
 Roli or kumkum
 Akshat (unbroken rice grains)
 Flowers
 Water in a karwa or kalash
 Fruits and sweets
 Incense sticks, if used
 A small quantity of wheat or other customary offerings
 A clean cloth for the puja area
 Some families also use a traditional drawing of Ahoi Mata, a syahu (porcupine) and her offspring as part of the ritual.
 Ahoi Ashtami Vrat Rules 
Ahoi Ashtami fasting practices vary across households and communities. The following are common traditions associated with the observance.
 Fasting: Many devotees observe a fast from morning until evening.
 Food and water: Some families follow a nirjala vrat, while others follow modified fasting practices.
 Evening puja: Ahoi Mata is worshipped during the evening, followed by the vrat katha.
 Tara darshan: Many devotees complete the fast after sighting stars and offering arghya.
 Moon worship: Some families wait until moonrise to complete the fast.
 Household customs: Rituals, food restrictions and puja materials may differ by region and family.
 Fasting is not suitable for everyone. Pregnant or breastfeeding women, people with diabetes or other medical conditions, and anyone taking medication that requires food or water should consult a healthcare professional before attempting a prolonged or waterless fast.
 Ahoi Ashtami Vrat Katha and Significance 
Ahoi Ashtami is associated with the traditional story of a mother who accidentally harms a young animal while digging the earth. The animal's mother, often described in the story as a syahu or porcupine, curses her with the loss of her children.
The woman later seeks forgiveness and prays with devotion. Ahoi Mata is associated with the restoration of her children's lives and the removal of her sorrow.
The story is traditionally recited during Ahoi Ashtami puja. It highlights themes of devotion, repentance, maternal love and the protection of children.
The vrat is observed by mothers who pray for their children's health, longevity, happiness and prosperity. While the observance was traditionally associated with sons in many communities, it is now commonly performed for the well-being of both sons and daughters.
 What Is the Significance of Ahoi Ashtami? 
Ahoi Ashtami is an important festival for families in North India. It is dedicated to Ahoi Mata, who is worshipped for the protection and well-being of children.
The festival is observed during Kartik Krishna Ashtami, and its evening rituals are closely associated with the sighting of stars. The vrat katha forms an important part of the observance, while the completion of the fast signifies the end of the day's prayers.
Ahoi Ashtami is also associated with Radha Kund in the Braj region. Some devotees visit Radha Kund for ritual bathing and prayers, particularly those seeking blessings related to children.
 Frequently Asked Questions 
 When is Ahoi Ashtami in 2026? 
 Ahoi Ashtami will be observed on Sunday, November 1, 2026. The festival falls on Kartik Krishna Ashtami and is traditionally observed by mothers for the well-being of their children.
 What is the Ahoi Ashtami puja muhurat in 2026? 
 Ahoi Ashtami puja muhurat in New Delhi is from 5:36 PM to 6:54 PM on November 1, 2026. Timings may vary by location.
 What is the Ahoi Ashtami tara darshan time in 2026? 
 Stars are expected to become visible at approximately 6:00 PM in New Delhi on November 1, 2026. The actual time may vary depending on the location and weather conditions.
 Is Ahoi Ashtami observed on November 1 or November 2 in 2026? 
 Ahoi Ashtami will be observed on November 1, 2026. Although the Ashtami Tithi continues into November 2, the evening observance and tara darshan take place on November 1.
 Can Ahoi Ashtami be observed for daughters? 
 Yes. Although the vrat was traditionally associated with prayers for sons in many communities, Ahoi Ashtami is now commonly observed for the health, happiness and long life of both sons and daughters.
